Although the Made by Google 2026 event officially kicks off in eight hours, Google has already fully disclosed all the details of the Pixel 11, Pixel Watch 5, and Pixel Tag.

Below is a summary of the announcements from Made by Google 2026. Each section includes links to our full hands-on coverage of the new hardware and software features, with more articles to come in the hours ahead.

Table of Contents

Pixel 11

The Pixel 11 features an all-glass camera bar design that is 40% thinner than the previous generation, with noticeably less protrusion. Google promotes that when used with the official case, this "platform" almost "disappears."

It comes with a larger 48-megapixel wide-angle sensor offering 56% greater light sensitivity and a slightly wider field of view. The Tensor G6 pairs with a 5x telephoto lens to deliver 30x SuperRes Zoom.

The processor is paired with 12 GB of RAM and 256 GB of storage, which is the new base configuration. This year's entry-level model supports 25W Qi2.2 wireless charging (up from 15W last generation), a 25% speed increase, while the officially claimed 30+ hour battery life remains unchanged.

The Pixel 11 is available in four colors: Frost, Obsidian, Hibiscus, and Pistachio, starting at $899.

Hands-on | Pre-order: Google Store — Amazon — Best Buy

Pixel 11 Pro and 11 Pro XL

The Pro series features an edge-to-edge camera bar with a built-in feature Google calls "HiLight." After three generations of replacing the temperature sensor, what surrounds the flash is a ring of ambient LEDs. It is designed to help users stay connected when the Pixel 11 Pro is placed face down. For example, it provides visual feedback through different modes to show when Gemini is listening, thinking, or responding, much like a Google Home smart speaker. You can also set custom colors that flash when a close contact calls (Phone by Google and WhatsApp), with future updates adding more features such as message notifications. You can enable HiLight and set one of five colors on the contact's Google Contacts page.

  • The Pixel 11 Pro features Google's most advanced Gemini Intelligence, starting at $1,099 [Hands-on]
  • Pixel 11 Pro's HiLight launches with just two features, with more to come

The Pixel 11 Pro and 11 Pro XL feature a new 50-megapixel wide-angle sensor and a 48-megapixel telephoto lens with a larger image sensor and 30% improved light sensitivity. This enables 5x portrait mode and achieves 120x Pro Zoom through the Tensor G6 and Google's latest imaging model. The processor and redesigned software also deliver Instant Night Sight up to 4.5x faster.

The Super Actua display peaks at 3,600 nits and features a new coating with 2x improved scratch resistance.

The Tensor G6 is paired with 12 GB of RAM on the 256 GB model. Regarding the 4 GB RAM reduction, Google says that through software and chip optimizations, performance is faster and smoother than last year's Pro model. However, you can upgrade to 16 GB of RAM by choosing the 512 GB or 1 TB version.

On the 11 Pro XL, faster wired charging can reach 75% in about 30 minutes, while wireless charging sees a 29% speed boost via 25W Qi2.2.

The phones are available in Canyon, Fog, Olive, and a first-ever all-matte Obsidian, with design inspiration drawn from nature. The 6.3-inch Pixel 11 Pro starts at $1,099, while the 6.8-inch Pixel 11 Pro XL starts at $1,299. On Pro models, Google now only offers six months of AI Pro access.

Hands-on | Pre-order:

Amazon: Pixel 11 Pro | 11 Pro XL

Pixel 11 Pro Fold

The Pixel 11 Pro Fold is nearly 10% lighter than last year's model (258g vs. 239g) and 0.7mm thinner. This foldable features a new matte fiberglass composite back offering 3x improved durability, billed as "nearly impossible to crack." A redesigned hinge protects the internal display from accidental drops.

The 6.5-inch external display is now upgraded to Super Actua (20% brighter) and protected by glass ceramic material. The internal Super Actua Flex display (also peaking at 3,600 nits) has slimmer bezels and uses thicker ultra-thin glass with a dual-layer impact-resistant film for improved crease performance.

The new 48-megapixel wide-angle sensor delivers 56% improved light sensitivity, while the telephoto lens supports 30x Super Zoom. You'll also find the HiLight feature on the Pixel 11 Pro Fold.

The Tensor G6 is paired with 16 GB of RAM and 256 GB of storage. The battery shrinks from 5,015 mAh to 4,750 mAh, but still maintains a 24+ hour usage rating and supports 25W Qi2.2 wireless charging.

Gboard's real-time transcription now supports American Sign Language. Sign-to-Text lets you "sign in front of the front camera while showing transcription on the external display." Combined with Android 17's Bubble Bar at the bottom-right corner, along with two new Made You Look animations in the camera app.

The Pixel 11 Pro Fold sees a $100 price increase to $1,899, but still offers 16 GB of RAM and 256 GB of storage.

Tensor G6

The new Gemini Nano 4 model benefits from the TPU, delivering 50% greater compute power and 2x memory bandwidth. This results in up to 3.5x faster on-device AI tasks while consuming up to 3.5x less energy.

Meanwhile, the CPU delivers 15% faster app launches and 25% faster web browsing.

The upgraded ISP (Image Signal Processor) unlocks more camera features, including wider zoom range and improved low-light performance. A new custom accelerator is designed for capturing and rendering portrait video, supporting 4K bokeh video.

The new Titan M3 security chip will help defend against future quantum computing threats.

New Pixel Camera and Video Features

While the camera app looks largely the same, Google has made several changes to accommodate new features. For example, quick access controls are no longer limited to white balance, exposure, and shadows, adding Looks, focus, shutter speed, and ISO sliders. The new interface lets you choose which apps to display on the left and right edges of the viewfinder after a tap.

  • Pixel 11 camera features new main sensor, "Camera Looks," "Instant Night Sight" and more
  • Pixel 11 videography upgrades with Pro Stable Video, Creator Suite and more

Magic Capture is somewhat like Google Clips — you simply start a capture session and Google picks the best HDR+ photos and videos. It can be accessed from a new capture mode tab (next to camera and video modes), analyzing about 500 frames to find the best shots and offering optional cropping, straightening, blur fixing, and other light edits. The goal is to let you simply point at the scene and focus on the moment.

Camera Looks let you set preset image styles when shooting. Google has adjusted the camera processing pipeline, such as "merging fewer frames than usual for a minimally processed feel" and "rewriting the color look-up table at the sensor level to mimic classic film chemistry." The Pixel 11 offers the following alternative HDR options:

  • Natural: relaxed detail feel
  • Shadows: stronger contrast
  • Vanilla: softer, warmer tones with a golden hue

There are also Stylistic Looks including Digi, Black Tie, Minimal, Editorial, Classic, and Velvet, which users can further customize.

On-device video processing has been improved in sharpening, noise reduction, and detail handling, while Pro Stable Video on the Pixel 11 Pro activates in shaky, well-lit scenes. The new Creator Suite adds several tools to the camera app:

  • Teleprompter: scrolls at your speaking pace, adjusting for speech rate and pauses
  • Project Folders: store clips to designated locations
  • Audio Visualizer: for checking microphones in the camera viewfinder
  • Storyboard: edit and rearrange clips through Google Photos
  • Social Media Grid Lines

Gemini Intelligence

The Pixel 11 series' workflow automation supports more apps, letting you outsource orders and reservations. Gemini can also call merchants to complete tasks.

Gboard Rambler goes beyond simple speech-to-text, filtering out lengthy sentences and filler words like "um" or "uh." Once activated, Rambler takes over Gboard's suggestion bar with a new waveform animation. It captures your intent and outputs clean, clear speech-to-text transcriptions.

Proactive Assistance (formerly Magic Cue) offers contextual suggestions with broader scenario support and a richer interface. When you tap these suggestions, a new bottom menu pops up. You can see rich flight details linked to live status, Google Maps business info, calendar previews when scheduling, tasks (like restaurant reservations), and various comparisons. Gemini Intelligence can also suggest saving events to your calendar and other data to Google Wallet.

Google is previewing a new At a Glance feature that detects your location to show membership cards when in stores and Google Maps business info when at restaurants.

Live Translate, which launched in calls last year, now expands to podcasts and videos in YouTube and other supported apps, delivering real-time audio dubbing via the Tensor G6.

New Pixelsnap Accessories

The latest Pixelsnap Cases match phone colors, and this year also adds a Clear Case. The Pixelsnap Ring Stand is now available in Canyon, Olive, and Obsidian.

Hands-on | Pre-order: Google Store — Amazon

Pixel Tag

The Google Pixel Tag is a Find Hub tracker priced at $29 (or $99 for a four-pack). It has a pill shape with a "G" logo on the back and a removable coin-cell battery. This accessory won't go on sale until November 11.

Pixel Buds Pro 2 Update

The Pixel Buds Pro 2 adds a new Olive colorway. More importantly, the Pixel Buds Pro 2 and Pixel Buds 2a will receive a major software update in September. The new Pro 2 firmware improves noise cancellation based on how well the earbuds seal in the ear canal. Google says it will "automatically adjust to compensate for slight changes in seal."

Meanwhile, the Pixel Buds Pro 2 and Pixel Buds 2a will add Gemini audio controls, letting you adjust settings via voice commands like "Hey Google, increase the bass."

The Pixel Watch sleep sync feature detects when you fall asleep to pause music, disable touch, and silence notifications. The upgraded instant translation lets you tap to "activate listening mode and understand over 70 languages in near real-time."

Pixel Watch 5

The Pixel Watch 5 looks the same as last year externally. Internally, it features the Snapdragon W5 Gen 2 Accelerated processor with 12% greater CPU compute power and RAM increased from 2 GB to 3 GB. These upgrades, combined with the M55 co-processor, deliver 20% overall speed improvement. Google has also doubled storage to 64 GB.

The Pixel Watch 5 delivers 2x improved route tracking and map accuracy in urban areas, hiking trails, and other complex environments. Google says its performance surpasses the Apple Watch Ultra 3 and Garmin Fenix 8 Pro.

  • Pixel Watch 5 looks familiar at first glance, but dig into At a Glance and you'll find surprises [Hands-on]
  • Pixel Watch 5 launches exclusive "Stephen Curry Edition" with unique band and watch face [Gallery]
  • Pixel Watch 5 features "second-generation Active Band" — here's what's changed and why you should get one

This year's health upgrades include enhanced strength training and HIIT experiences, the introduction of Bedtime Automations, new Breathing Emergency Detection, and support for blood pressure and insulin resistance trend tracking.

Mckillio's top comment

Slightly better than I expected, especially on the camera side (except the front camera), but still not enough to make me upgrade, especially since I have to buy 512 GB to get 16 GB of RAM, and I don't even need 256 GB. Unless reviews are absolutely stellar, I'll keep waiting for the 12P.

This year adds two new watch faces — Weave and Chronograph — along with new complication styles. You can also use generative UI watch faces that feel like AI wallpapers on your phone.

Gemini Intelligence brings At a Glance to the bottom of the watch face, displaying flight details, boarding passes, and transit station info. Proactive Suggestions can be presented as one-tap actions in apps like Google Messages. Offline Gemini command support lets you control timers and alarms, and start workout sessions.

The Pixel Watch 5 starts at $399, with the 41mm version ($50 more) and 45mm version ($30 more), adding cellular connectivity for an extra $100.
